conjectures: A single-pair disequality probe at k=5 is a weak instrument on this object: 30703 of 149906 non-adjacent pairs are already equal-coloured in one witness, and a 5-colouring was found in well under a second, so the k=5 colouring space is very large. The honest reading of the SAT outcome is 'no evidence of forcing at this pair', not 'no forcing in this graph'.

If any forced-equality pair at k=5 exists in this coordinate set it is unlikely to be found by probing individual pairs chosen from one witness colouring; a better probe would target pairs that are equal in ALL of several independent witness colourings (a necessary condition for forcing), which is still a bounded and cheap filter.
Escape from the palette cap of Theorem B still requires some mechanism other than a common-neighbour exclusion; a cascade of length >= 2 is one such route and is not claimed to be exhaustive.

escalation.obstacle: Is there a finite unit-distance graph with two marks p,q at distance d != 1 such that G is k-colourable but G+pq is not, for k = 4, 5 or 6, where the forcing does not arise from excluding a common neighbourhood? Theorems A and B show the two analysed operators cannot produce one for k >= 4. I have not constructed one, ran no literature audit, and have no exhaustive classification of escape routes.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. Diamond: K_4 minus an edge, vertices a,b,t1,t2, edges ab, at1, at2, bt1, bt2, |t1-t2| = sqrt3. Palette excluder for a non-adjacent pair (p,q): a clique S with every s in S adjacent to both p and q.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite graph; no measurability, periodicity or lattice hypothesis.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Clique-interface gluing (Theorem A); palette exclusion via common neighbours (Theorem B, sharp at k=3 by the diamond); stacking common-unit-neighbour gadgets (the operation is an involution); exhaustive forced-pair census on the block-1 spindle family; a 553-vertex census confirming Theorems B and C on real data; and now one pre-registered single-pair disequality probe at k=5, which returned SAT.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either an explicit exact-coordinate gadget of modest size forcing equality at k=4, together with the graph-theoretic mechanism by which it evades Theorem B (a cascade or some other route, stated precisely), or a proof that any such gadget must have at least N(k) vertices, with N(k) stated as a function of k together with the exact argument producing the bound and the point at which the argument fails.
